transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2025-10-08 15:00 UTC
- Duration: ~62 minutes
- Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE); Ravi Patel (Redwood SE); Liam Park (Redwood Solutions Eng); Sofia Alvarez (Helio, Lead ML); Tom Reyes (Helio, DevOps); Priya Singh (Helio, Product); Carlos Mendez (CTO, joined 15m in)

Summary (auto): 0:00 - quick intros, 04:30 - SDK install + auth walkthrough, 18:00 - Console tour, 31:00 - Optimize recommendations and performance notes, 44:00 - Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private discussion, 55:00 - recap and next steps.

00:00 Maya: All right, hey everyone thanks for joining, um this is Maya from Redwood, i'm the AE on the account, joining with Ravi our SE and Liam from solutions. can you do quick intros from your side?
00:12 Sofia: Hi, i'm Sofia, lead ML engineer on HelioMetrics, we own the inference pipelines and model infra.
00:17 Tom: Tom, devops, will handle network and infra side.
00:20 Priya: Priya, product — i'm helping prioritize the pilot.
00:23 Ravi: Cool thanks. quick agenda: SDK quickstart in py/ts, auth patterns, console and optimize tips, then Q&A and next steps.
00:33 Maya: Great, one thing before we start—any hard constraints we should know about latency or data residency?
00:40 Sofia: We're looking at sub-200ms for short completions, and overall we want cost predictability. also need to know if we can keep telemetry data in eu-west for gdpr.
00:50 Tom: And we need to validate VPC peering or private link, can't accept egress to unknown endpoints in prod.
00:57 Maya: Perfect, we'll cover Private options and VPC.
01:05 Ravi: ok moving into the SDK — i'll share my screen, starting with pip install redwood-sdk, and node install @redwood/sdk for ts. a quick note: the SDK supports both sync and streaming responses.
01:25 Ravi: (typing) for python, set REDWOOD_API_KEY in your env var, we show export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk-XXXX. there is also support for vault/KMS. some teams use our built-in key rotation with customer-managed keys.
01:45 Priya: when you say KMS, is that AWS KMS? we use GCP KMS at Helio.
01:50 Ravi: yes we support a range — aws/gcp/azure and customer HSMs. note: in Private mode the key material can remain in your KMS via our connector.
02:05 Sofia: can you show the TS example for auth? we've got a lot of front-end code in node.
02:12 Ravi: sure — for node we suggest process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY or using a short-lived token from our auth service. you can also use service-to-service tokens minted via our CLI. (murmur) there was a small typo in our quickstart readme last week, it's fixed now.
02:30 Speaker 1: [crosstalk]
02:33 Tom: sorry, question — our security team requires no static API keys on instances. the recommended pattern?
02:38 Liam: fall through is to use our short-lived token flow: you run a small agent on your host that calls a token exchange endpoint and get ephemeral token, that minimizes blast radius. we demo that pattern in the repo.
02:50 Sofia: okay that sounds doable. can you show the CLI step for creating a sandbox env?
02:55 Ravi: yep. redwood sandbox create --name helio-qa --region eu-west-1. that'll provision a sandbox project with a sandbox key. we also generate console links for usage and route configs.
03:12 Sofia: does sandbox allow simulating Dedicated behavior?
03:15 Ravi: sort of — sandbox runs shared hosted infra but you can toggle concurrency and token limits to mimic Dedicated throughput; for true dedicated you'd spin up Redwood Dedicated pools. the sandbox won't replicate strict isolation.
03:28 Priya: how long does Dedicated provisioning take, roughly?
03:30 Maya: typical is 2-3 weeks for contractual and infra setup, sometimes quicker with existing region capacity.
03:36 Carlos: (joins) hey folks, sorry i'm late — quick summary?
03:40 Maya: we are in SDK auth + env setup, then Console. we'll also cover Optimize later.
04:00 Ravi: jumping to Console — note the token-level cost breakdown per route, per model, and our Console shows latency percentiles and token histograms. screen: route-level view -> you can set per-route model pins and fallbacks.
04:30 Sofia: are these traces accessible via our existing datadog?
04:34 Ravi: yes we have tracing webhooks and a raw export; you can forward traces to datadog or use our tracing API. the console also has downloadable CSVs.
04:48 Tom: security logs/audit? we need proof for SOC2.
04:52 Maya: full audit trails are available on Private and Dedicated, and hosted has 90-day audit logs depending on plan. we'll share the SOC2 doc.
05:05 Priya: Optimize — can you give quick wins to lower token costs?
05:10 Ravi: sure — automatic prefix caching (we call it KV caching in the docs but sometimes transcribed as K-V cash) for repeated prompts; smarter batching windows; and quantization recommendations. we'll run a lightweight analyze job on sample traffic and the Optimize console suggests the quantization profile.
05:28 Sofia: does quant'd model reduce latency? sometimes it increases CPU decoding time.
05:32 Ravi: depends on architecture — lower-bit int ops reduce memory and can improve throughput but single-request latency can vary. Optimize provides per-model perf profiles so you can pick the right tradeoff.
05:45 Tom: can we run a tiny benchmark from our infra? we prefer to run with our internal dataset.
05:50 Ravi: absolutely — next week we can run a short bench (50k tokens) on hosted and a Dedicated sim; i'll coordinate with you for the harness.
06:02 Sofia: quick technical: how does Redwood handle KV cache across request replicas? if we're using autoscaling pools, consistency is a concern.
06:12 Ravi: currently KV cache is per-node, with a smart prefix cache in the request router — for Dedicated we can expose a shared KV cache layer if required. note that cache locality matters for latency.
06:25 Sofia: make note: Helio needs strong cache locality to hit p50 under 150ms for common prompts.
06:32 Maya: noted.
06:40 Ravi: demo time — i'll run the simple python quickstart that calls text generation. (screen) code: from redwood import Client; c = Client(); c.generate("Summarize: ..."). Logan the transcript here shows streaming in chat.
06:58 (short pause, typing noises)
07:10 Ravi: small hiccup — my local env var pointed to sandbox-old, ignore that. switching keys.
07:28 Sofia: that's fine, dev life.
07:35 Ravi: ok streaming shows tokens as they arrive, you can hook into on_token and on_complete events. for node, it's the same API semantics with streams.
07:50 Tom: do you have a quick example of how to instrument token cost attribution in our app?
07:55 Ravi: yes — we expose token metadata per response and the SDK emits a usage header you can parse and post to your billing bucket, or send via ingestion to your cost service.
08:12 Priya: any pitfalls with our existing rate limits? we have spike traffic.
08:16 Maya: we recommend route-level bursts and autoscale policies; if spikes are predictable you can pre-warm Dedicated or use burst capacity add-on.
08:28 Sofia: security question — for Private/on-prem deployments, do you require the console to be reachable or is control plane optional?
08:35 Liam: Private has optional control plane connectivity. you can run fully air-gapped with the on-prem agent, we ship an admin bundle and a local console.
08:45 Tom: good. for VPC peering — do you support shared services VPC or only peering?
08:50 Ravi: both. we can do VPC peering, PrivateLink, or a transit gateway approach. depends on your cloud provider. we'll share the network diagrams.
09:02 Carlos: about pilot success — what should we agree on as acceptance criteria?
09:06 Sofia: for the pilot Helio wants: 1) <200ms p50 for primary prompts with caching, 2) cost within 15% of our target, 3) no PII leaving eu region during the trial (data residency).
09:18 Maya: perfect — we'll build the pilot plan around that.
09:25 Ravi: i'll propose an A/B harness to test hosted vs dedicated simulation. we'll instrument traces and token cost.
09:32 Priya: timeline? we want to present to execs by 10/24.
09:36 Maya: ok pilot kickoff 10/15, 2 week pilot and final exec summary 10/24 works — tight but doable.
09:43 Tom: what about pricing — can we get a ballpark for 50k tokens a month and a small Dedicated node?
09:48 Maya: i'll send an estimate — hosted per token + optional reserved for Dedicated; i'll include a committed spend scenario.
09:55 Sofia: there was a comment earlier about model fallbacks — can you show how to set automatic fallback to cheaper model when high load?
10:00 Ravi: yes in Console under routing policies you can set fallback chains and cost thresholds — if latency SLO is at risk we can fallback to a smaller quantized variant automatically.
10:12 (brief screen share of console routing)
10:25 Priya: will that preserve the KV cache or will it warm a new cache for the fallback model?
10:30 Ravi: it's model-dependent — fallback often needs cache warming; we have a hybrid approach where we warm critical prefixes. Optimize can precompute warm-up batches.
10:40 Sofia: okay good.
10:45 Maya: i'm going to summarize next steps — and assign owners.
10:50 Maya: Action items recap: Maya will send sandbox invite and the SOC2 + network diagrams. Ravi will run the sample bench and share SDK snippets. Tom to confirm VPC constraints. and schedule the 10/15 pilot kickoff.
11:05 Carlos: quick ask — can Redwood run the first bench from your infra and share logs so our security can review?
11:10 Ravi: yes we can run a hosted bench in eu-west and share sanitized logs; for deeper review we can set a joint test on Private.
11:20 Priya: perfect.
11:30 Maya: any final Qs?
11:33 Tom: one more — do you have a quick doc on tokenization differences across models? we use that to estimate costs.
11:38 Ravi: will include the tokenization guide in the packet.
11:45 Sofia: ok thanks everyone, this was helpful.
11:50 Maya: thanks all, we'll follow up with materials and the pilot timeline.
11:55 (meeting ends)
